Maysa was the chattiest girl in the class. Whenever she spoke, the girls laughed and gathered around her, and she loved that.

Hala sat in the seat in front of her. She was calm and did not talk much.

One cold day, Maysa walked past Hala's house. Through the door she saw Hala's mother mending an old coat that had belonged to her big sister, saying, "Wear this one this winter, Hala, until your father finds work."

Maysa walked on, and Hala did not see her.

In the morning, Hala came into class in the old coat. It was too long for her, and the sleeves covered her fingers.

Ranim whispered to Maysa, "Why is Hala wearing a coat that's too big for her?"

Maysa knew the answer, and she could feel it on the tip of her tongue.

If she said it, the girls would laugh and gather around her as they did every day, and she would be the one with the news.

But she remembered a hadith their teacher had read that morning: "Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him say something good or keep quiet."

So she kept quiet.

Ranim said, "You know something — I can see it on your face!"

Maysa said, "All I'll say about it is that it's a lovely colour."

Then she opened her book as if she were reading.

At break time, Hala sat alone in a corner of the playground, her hands tucked into the long sleeves of the coat.

Maysa went to her, sat down beside her, and shared her sandwich with her, without asking her anything.

A few days later, Hala said quietly, "My mum said you walked past our house that day."

Then she said, "I was scared the whole class would find out… and nobody did."

Maysa said, "And nobody will."

Hala smiled for the first time in days, and wiped her eyes with the end of her long sleeve.

From that day on, Maysa asked herself before she spoke, "Is this a good word?"

And Hala sat beside her at every break.

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him say something good or keep quiet."

📖 Agreed upon (Al-Bukhari and Muslim). This is a tale told as a parable; it did not happen to anyone in particular.
